diagnostics.message: module.eks_blueprints.module.emr_on_eks:resource.null_resource.update_trust_policy: explicit depends_on of module.eks_blueprints.module.emr_on_eks:resource.aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.eks_blueprints.module.emr_on_eks:resource.null_resource.update_trust_policy: explicit depends_on of module.eks_blueprints.module.emr_on_eks:resource.kubernetes_namespace.spark is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.eks_blueprints.module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng: explicit depends_on of module.eks_blueprints.module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_role.managed_ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.eks_blueprints.module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng: explicit depends_on of module.eks_blueprints.module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.eks_blueprints.module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng: explicit depends_on of module.eks_blueprints.module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references

`aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng` already depends on `aws_iam_role.managed_ng` implicitly through `node_role_arn = ... aws_iam_role.managed_ng[0].arn`, so the extra `depends_on` entry for that role is redundant (the `aws_iam_instance_profile.managed_ng` and `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng` entries are not redundant and should stay).

`null_resource.update_trust_policy` already references `kubernetes_namespace.spark.id` inside its local-exec command (`--namespace ${kubernetes_namespace.spark.id}`), which is an ordinary attribute reference that orders it after the namespace; listing the namespace in `depends_on` duplicates that edge.

`null_resource.update_trust_policy` already references `aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id` inside its local-exec command (`--role-name ${aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id}`), so the explicit `depends_on` on that role duplicates the implicit attribute-reference edge.

The Prometheus add-on creates `kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus` (when `create_namespace` is true, which is the default here) but passes only the plain string `local.namespace_name` to `module.helm_addon` and sets `create_namespace = false` on the chart, so nothing orders the Helm release after the namespace. Unlike the other add-on modules (agones, traefik, vpa, metrics-server, ...), `helm_addon` here has no `depends_on = [kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus]`, so `helm_release.addon` can be installed into a namespace that has not been created yet. Add an explicit dependency (or wire the created namespace's name into the release config) so the namespace exists first.
